sections.h2: Where is Baldwin County, Alabama, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Baldwin County sits in the southwestern corner of Alabama on the Gulf coast, on the eastern side of Mobile Bay. According to its Wikipedia entry, it is the largest county in the state by area, at 2,027 square miles in total, of which 1,590 are land. The county seat is Bay Minette, while Daphne is the largest city.

Locals describe the county in regions: North Baldwin, the Eastern Shore, Central Baldwin, South Baldwin, Southwest Baldwin and East Baldwin. Central Baldwin is the strip along State Route 59 from the Interstate 10 exit at Loxley through Robertsdale to Summerdale. The Census Bureau splits the county into subdivisions centered on Bay Minette, Daphne, Elberta, Fairhope, Foley, Robertsdale, Stockton and Summerdale.

If you own a house here, the first thing to know is which of these areas it is in. The county has three public school districts: Baldwin County, Gulf Shores City and Orange Beach City, the last formed in 2022. A house in Orange Beach and one in Bay Minette are in the same county but not the same school system.

sections.h2: What cities and towns are in Baldwin County?
sections.html:
The county lists nine cities and five towns. The cities are Bay Minette, Daphne, Fairhope, Foley, Gulf Shores, Loxley, Orange Beach, Robertsdale and Spanish Fort. The towns are Elberta, Magnolia Springs, Perdido Beach, Silverhill and Summerdale.

There are also unincorporated places and census designated places such as Point Clear, Fort Morgan, Bon Secour, Lillian, Stapleton and Stockton. Check your tax bill to see which levies apply to your address.

  • The Foley subdivision includes Gulf Shores, Magnolia Springs and most of Orange Beach.
  • The Daphne subdivision includes Spanish Fort.
  • The Robertsdale subdivision includes Loxley and Silverhill.
  • The Elberta subdivision includes Perdido Beach.

sections.h2: How fast has Baldwin County grown, and what does that mean for a house seller?
sections.html:
Baldwin was Alabama's fastest-growing county from 2010 to 2020, per the same source, and four of the state's ten fastest-growing cities were in it. The population went from 182,265 in 2010 to 231,767 in 2020. Of the 124,148 housing units counted in the 2020 census, 25.0 percent were vacant.

Growth is uneven. The Foley subdivision grew from 48,089 to 64,862 people between 2010 and 2020, and the Daphne subdivision, which includes Spanish Fort, went from 41,295 to 55,767. The Stockton area was nearly flat, at 3,804 and 3,745.

For a seller, that spread means two different markets under one county name. Check the numbers for your own part of the county rather than the county average. Our cash offers reflect the condition and location of the specific house.

sections.h2: What is the climate risk for a Baldwin County house?
sections.html:
Baldwin frequently endures tropical weather systems, and the county has been declared a disaster area several times. Wikipedia lists Hurricane Frederic in September 1979, Danny in July 1997, Georges in September 1998, Ivan in September 2004, Katrina in August 2005 and Sally in September 2020.

That history shapes what a buyer looks at on a coastal house: roof condition, wind and flood coverage, drainage and any storm repair that is half done. A property that has been through a named storm and has an open insurance claim or unrepaired damage is a very different sale from a tidy one.

Cash sales are one way owners avoid the delay of repair loans, appraisals tied to condition, and buyers who back out after an inspection. We purchase houses as they stand, including storm-damaged ones.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and airports shape a Baldwin County sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 10 and Interstate 65 cross the county, along with U.S. Highways 31, 90 and 98 and State Routes 59, 104, 180, 181, 182, 225 and 287. The Baldwin Beach Express is also listed. Loxley is described as growing as a suburb of Daphne and Spanish Fort because it has an Interstate 10 exit and sits roughly between Mobile and Pensacola.

The county has airports at Bay Minette, Fairhope, Foley and Gulf Shores, but commercial scheduled service comes from Mobile Regional Airport, Mobile Downtown Airport or Pensacola International Airport. Coastal Alabama Community College has several campuses in the county, and the United States Sports Academy is in Daphne.

Part of Wolf Bay and 42 miles of the Tensaw River were designated Outstanding Alabama Water, and part of the Bon Secour National Wildlife Refuge lies in the county. If your house is near water, keep your survey and any flood certificate handy.

sections.h2: How is property tax handled by the Baldwin County Revenue Commission?
sections.html:
Baldwin has an elected revenue commissioner who serves the whole county. The Collections Division collects tax on all real and personal property assessed in the county, and its page says taxes are due October 1 each year. Courtesy notices usually go out before then so owners can check their mailing address.

Taxes are delinquent after December 31. Penalties and interest begin to accrue after that date, and the owner has to contact Collections to learn the new amount due. Personal and business checks are accepted between October 1 and February 28. The collections phone number on the page is 251-937-0245.

If a mortgage company pays your tax through escrow, the page says it is still the owner's responsibility to confirm the payment was made. The county offers an EscrowCheck tool that shows the real-time status of escrow payments from banks and lenders, using the parcel number without dashes.

  • October 1: taxes due.
  • December 31: last day before delinquency.
  • February 28: last day for personal and business checks.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Baldwin County property valuation?
sections.html:
The Revenue Commission's FAQ lists questions on how to protest an appraised value, whether a protest can be filed by phone, what happens if you miss your hearing, and why you might not have received a valuation notice. It also links to a fillable online protest form. The FAQ page collapses the answers, so open it and expand the questions for the current instructions.

One question on that page is worth quoting by topic: the valuation notice is not your tax bill. Owners sometimes mix the two. A notice states the appraised value and starts the protest clock, while the bill arrives for the October 1 due date.

If you plan to sell, do not let an appraisal protest wait. A buyer's title company will want the tax record current, and a pending protest can leave the amount unsettled at closing.

sections.h2: What happens in Baldwin County when taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The Revenue Commission's tax lien auction page explains that Alabama's 2018 legislature passed Act 2018-577, an alternative to selling the property: selling the tax lien. Baldwin migrated to lien sales in 2019 beginning with tax year 2018 delinquent properties. All liens for unpaid and delinquent real property taxes are subject to a public auction.

The county's FAQ list for that auction asks the questions an owner would ask. Is ownership transferred when a lien is bought? How do you redeem a lien? What happens to liens that do not sell? The auction uses the GovEase platform, and the page lists one question on whether training is available for it. The answers are on the county page, so read them before you decide anything.

State redemption rules still matter. Our Alabama tax sale page summarizes who can redeem and how long they have.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Baldwin County with tax due?
sections.html:
The title company pays the delinquent tax, and any lien redemption amount, from your proceeds at closing. You supply the parcel number, the tax years owed and a payoff figure from Collections.

If the county sold a lien on your parcel, ask Collections what the payoff includes. Request the figure in writing, and give the title company enough time to confirm it.

We buy Baldwin County houses as they are, including ones with delinquent tax, storm damage or deferred repairs.

faqs.q: When are Baldwin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1 each year. They become delinquent after December 31, and penalties and interest accrue after that date.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Baldwin County?
faqs.a: The Baldwin County Revenue Commission's Collections Division. Its page lists 251-937-0245 as the collections phone number.

faqs.q: What if my mortgage company pays my Baldwin County tax?
faqs.a: Confirm that it did. The Revenue Commission says that is the owner's responsibility, and its EscrowCheck tool shows whether an escrow payment reached the county.

faqs.q: Does Baldwin County sell tax liens or the property itself?
faqs.a: Liens. The Revenue Commission says it began selling tax liens in 2019 with tax year 2018 delinquents under Act 2018-577, and all liens for unpaid real property taxes are subject to public auction.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Baldwin County?
faqs.a: Bay Minette. Daphne is the largest city, and the county sits on the eastern side of Mobile Bay.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Baldwin County house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. The tax and any lien payoff are paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Collections Division first.
